chief_complaint: Management of hypertension and obesity with associated prediabetes
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 39-year-old woman with a history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2019, obesity (BMI ≥30) noted in 2023, and prediabetes (A1c 6.2%) documented since 2016. Blood pressure at the most recent visit was 128/90 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension) and heart rate 98 bpm. She also has chronic sinusitis, anemia of unspecified type, and is receiving vitamin B12 injections. Social factors include housing instability, social isolation, and involvement in risk activities. She is currently employed full‑time and has completed higher education. She attends regular wellness visits (10 of 43 total visits) but recent labs lack lipid profile, renal function, and detailed anemia work‑up. Current medications are hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily and vitamin B12 injections.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple episodes of gingivitis (2021‑2023) and a tooth infection resolved in May 2023, prior periods of not being in the labor force (resolved 2023), past reports of environmental violence (resolved 2022), previous stress (resolved 2023), and earlier documentation of full‑time employment (resolved 2022).

active_medications.name: Vitamin B12 5 MG/ML Injectable Solution
active_medications.purpose: Management of anemia presumed due to B12 deficiency

social_determinants: Housing unsatisfactory, social isolation, involvement in risk activities, full‑time employment, higher education; no documented smoking, alcohol, or substance use status.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 2 hypertension (BP 128/90), obesity (BMI ≥30), prediabetes (A1c 6.2%), elevated resting heart rate (98 bpm). Metabolic risk: prediabetes, possible dyslipidaemia (lipid panel missing). Hematologic risk: anemia with B12 therapy suggesting macrocytic component. ENT risk: chronic sinusitis. Renal risk cannot be assessed (eGFR missing). Psychosocial risk: housing instability, social isolation, risk activity involvement. Charlson comorbidity index 1, clinical complexity moderate.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with moderate clinical complexity driven by cardiometabolic risk factors (stage 2 hypertension, obesity, prediabetes) and anemia, compounded by significant social determinants of health such as housing instability and social isolation. Current therapy appears suboptimal for blood pressure control and metabolic risk, and key laboratory assessments are missing, limiting full risk stratification.
